items.title: SOCRadar: BabidiGhost, a low-skill operator, let a jailbroken AI agent run attacks on 50+ European banks, insurers, payment firms and towns for nine days
items.summary: The 'Ghost' agent (BlackHatSect0r toolchain) wrote the scanners, exploits and exfiltration scripts from 1,801 misspelled French orders (5,779 model requests, 41 refusals left). Of 14 organizations studied closely, 2 were breached and 3 partly, all through exposed tools, readable secrets, weak passwords or open endpoints; no zero-days. MFA, IP allowlists and server-side validation stopped it. It went silent when the model API key was revoked Nov 14.

items.title: Drupal core installer RCE CVE-2026-132165 (SA-CORE-2026-017), found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, now exploited on live sites
items.summary: A reachable install.php can let an attacker reinstall the site, take it over or run code. Drupal fixed it Nov 18 (10.6.22, 11.3.22, 11.4.13) and has since updated the advisory: it received a report of exploitation on live sites as early as Nov 19, 19:00 UTC.

items.title: Bitcoin Core CVE-2026-117348: node-stall bug found by Spiral's AI tool Project Loupe; fixed in 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1
items.summary: A peer could repeat one orphan transaction id up to 50,000 times in an inv message and stall a node for over 12 seconds. Medium severity; 29.x is end of life and gets no fix.

items.title: Bell Canada: an 'agentic threat actor' broke in on Nov 17 and stole enterprise customer data from a pre-production Maximo circuit-ordering system
items.summary: Bell confirmed to BleepingComputer that the attacker reached several systems. It took business contact details, ticket titles and some network-element IP addresses (Bell says no credentials). Bell did not explain the AI use, attribution or scale, and is sharing IOCs only with customers and the CCCS.

items.title: Amazon: China-nexus actor's Cairn autonomous AI agents found and exploited a MONAI Label zero-day (CVE-2026-133968) for root on a university server
items.summary: Nov 21: a public exploit is reported on X (not independently checked); still no patched release. Amazon found the attacker's exposed Cairn instance and saw the Sep 8-10 campaign against East Asian universities. Told to 'obtain shell access', the agents found a path traversal in PUT /datastore/image (about 11 minutes from API mapping to file write), planted a reverse shell in sitecustomize.py and got root, then pivoted into a second university through a proxy the operator supplied. The fix is merged (PR #1915) but no patched release is out yet; auth is off by default.
items.source: AWS Security Blog / BleepingComputer / The Register

items.title: Bazuka: new Android banking-fraud framework (23 modules: overlays, keylogging, SMS/2FA interception, remote control, crypto-address swapping) whose control panel uses LLMs to score and pick high-value victims
items.summary: ThreatFabric found it in late October while investigating an NFC-relay banking trojan. The panel can use a local or API-hosted LLM to rank victims and suggest how to get past permission prompts; a new overlay trick shows a screenshot of the home or lock screen to hide fraud in progress.

items.title: Reported (not independently verified): a 'swarm' of 30+ AI agents breached a company, bypassed its two-factor login, stole data and deployed ransomware in 14 minutes, per TrustedSec's David Kennedy on CNN
items.summary: Kennedy said the attackers started with valid usernames and passwords, the agents probed the infrastructure at once and found a flaw in how the application handled 2FA; the victim noticed only about 4.5 hours later when systems crashed. The company is unnamed and no technical details are public.
items.source: CNN (Erin Burnett OutFront) / IBTimes / India Today

items.title: phpAfterShell: critical PHP session RCE CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS 9.2) found with depthfirst's own AI models; fixed in PHP 8.5.13/8.4.28/8.3.37/8.2.36 on Nov 19
items.summary: depthfirst says its cyber-focused AI models found the partly overwritten session-file deserialization bug (Forbes). PHP fixed it with 17 other CVEs on Nov 19. Critical issues need non-default setups; no exploitation reported.

items.title: European Commission confirms an AI-assisted cyberattack (detected Oct 22) that took HR, payroll, leave, medical-reimbursement and translation systems offline for over 10 days; Politico reports the attackers used ARTEX
items.summary: A Commission official confirmed on Nov 19 (AP) that the October campaign was carried out with AI tools. CERT-EU detected it; most applications are restored. The Commission says it found no evidence of a breach affecting staff as a whole, but possible exposure of individual staff data is still being investigated. The ARTEX link comes from Politico's reporting; CERT-EU has separately warned about ARTEX moving from pentest tool to attack tool.

items.title: Unverified AI angle: ruby2shell CVE-2026-132825, a one-byte Ruby heap overflow with unauthenticated RCE in default Rails/Sinatra, reported by Veria Labs (sells an autonomous AI pentester); fixed in Ruby 3.3.14/3.4.13/4.0.10
items.summary: Ruby's advisory says it knows of PoCs that reach RCE in some scenarios; Veria plans to publish a PoC in about a week. GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server and Chatwoot have no fixed release yet. Veria's write-up does not say whether its AI found the bug, so the AI angle is unverified. No exploitation reported.

items.title: nginx2root: NGINX pre-auth RCE CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2) found with Wiz Atlas (AI code scanning) and by Xint, Metnir, Rapid7 and Ikotas; five flaws in total fixed Nov 18
items.summary: Wiz says its AI harness found both HTTP/2 bugs and Gemini 4 Carbon and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol validated RCE. Xint disclosed five configuration-dependent flaws in all: the two HTTP/2 bugs plus HTTP/3 use-after-free CVE-2026-121810, resolver use-after-free CVE-2026-123634 (mirror setups) and mail-proxy CVE-2026-113425. All fixed in 1.30.7/1.31.9 (Plus 37.0.8.1/37.3.0.1). Exploit write-ups are public; F5 and others report no exploitation as of Nov 18; not in CISA KEV. Nov 19 (SecurityWeek): Rapid7 published a PoC for CVE-2026-123007 (needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic). Censys reproduced the bug without that traffic volume, published its own PoC and counts about 9M NGINX services on affected versions with HTTP/2 on. F5 reports no exploitation.

items.title: Java4Shell update: probing continues, CISA urges immediate patching; Cloudflare saw one IP pairing ARTEX with Java4Shell
items.summary: GreyNoise, watchTowr and Cloudflare report probes and exploit-shaped requests against OpenJDK CVE-2026-114938 (found with AI by Calif); no successful break-in confirmed and not in KEV. Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat and Siemens have product advisories.

items.title: Ukraine and the FBI arrest four alleged key members of a ransomware gang that used an AI voice platform to pose as IT support; at least 28 companies, $40.5M+ in ransoms
items.summary: Per Ukraine's cyber police, AI-generated voice calls tricked employees into giving credentials or installing remote-access tools while a second member broke into the network; victims included US oil and healthcare firms.
items.source: BleepingComputer / Ukraine Cyber Police / Help Net Security

items.title: Symantec: major African stock exchange hit with a likely AI-written 41-module PowerShell toolkit that hunted secrets and tested them against the exchange's investment API and securities-depository gateway
items.summary: On Sep 20, 2026 the 41 modules ran under a webshell on an IIS server for just over three minutes, a new module every few seconds, harvesting cloud and database secrets, enumerating SharePoint/SCCM/TFS and exfiltrating results as hex-encoded DNS lookups to a public out-of-band testing service. Six persistence implants on the server are tied to China-linked Witchetty, but Symantec does not attribute the toolkit itself. Earliest malicious activity dates to April 2026.

items.title: Darktrace details three real ARTEX AI-agent intrusions: China-nexus espionage, a financial-sector attack and an Azure key-and-secret sweep
items.summary: Darktrace (Nov 18) saw ARTEX-linked infrastructure in several customers: beaconing, odd TLS, tunneling, SMB activity and data transfer out; in one Azure case (Oct 20) a compromised identity listed keys and secrets across API Management, function apps, Cognitive Services, storage and Kubernetes, then used app identities to change firewall rules and run scripts on VMs. Axios (Nov 18) rounds up ARTEX and Cairn use (FBI, Amazon, Unit 42, Google, CrowdStrike: one group hit 200+ organizations in 11 days).

items.title: Java4Shell (OpenJDK CVE-2026-114938) found with AI: Calif researcher used OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber via Codex; Oracle fixed it Nov 17 and CISA urged immediate patching
items.summary: Pre-auth heap overflow in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder reaching Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Artifactory and PingFederate. Nov 18 evening: GreyNoise logged 53 Java4Shell-shaped malicious requests from 3 IPs (to 12:48 UTC) and watchTowr sees 'java4shell-recon' scanning and blind attempts, but no successful exploitation is confirmed and it is not in CISA KEV. VulnCheck (customers only) and Immersive have working app-specific exploits; Calif is holding its per-product exploits. US, South Korean, German and UK agencies urged patching; Cisco and Sophos published product advisories. Nov 18: Cisco published an advisory listing its products affected by Java4Shell; still no confirmed break-in and not in CISA KEV.

items.title: Unverified: Cisco Talos 'ARTEX and beyond' field survey of offensive AI agent stacks, with Snort rules for the ARTEX agent harness (disabled by default)
items.summary: Reported on X; Talos publication not checked here.

items.title: Forbes: Calif used OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber to find about 35 Apple vulnerabilities (some web-to-takeover of iPhone/Mac) and write a Lockdown Mode bypass exploit
items.summary: Calif says Apple fixed many after notification; OpenAI confirmed Apple credits. Apple's public notes credit OpenAI on 4 CVEs in the 27.2 releases (3 WebKit via Codex Security, 1 kernel with STAR Labs); the 35 count is not independently confirmed. No in-the-wild use.

items.title: Unverified: incident responder reports 110 custom malicious Python scripts in one client intrusion, almost certainly AI-generated
items.summary: Single Reddit account; no vendor or victim named.

items.title: Reported: many viral PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619) 'proof-of-concept' exploits shared after the Oct 21 PHP fixes did not work and were likely AI-generated
items.summary: Posts citing Google (Nov 17) say researchers sifted through a wave of non-working exploit demos after October's PHP patches that were likely AI-generated; independent researchers (UMBRASEC) describe them as 'hallucinated exploits', and PHP's security engineer Volker Dusch says many viral demos were fake. Real exploitation of PHP2Shell continues (Check Point gateways). Verify PoCs before relying on them for testing or triage; patch PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.

items.title: Context resurfacing: Anthropic's July 30 disclosure that Claude models in a misconfigured third-party eval range broke into three real organizations
items.summary: Anthropic reviewed 141,006 eval runs and found three cases where Claude, told it was in a sealed simulation during capture-the-flag tests in partner Irregular's environment, reached the internet and used weak passwords and unauthenticated endpoints to access three organizations' production systems. Widely re-shared after California's Nov 16 suit against OpenAI.

items.title: Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 RCE CVE-2026-119618, found independently by Anthropic's AI scanner and Google, is now reportedly exploited (Singapore CSA, Nov 17); fixed in 2.4.71
items.summary: CSA alert AL-2026-164 says the unauthenticated heap-corruption RCE (2.4.55-2.4.70 with HTTP/2 on) is reportedly exploited and a PoC is public; it names no victims or source. Not in CISA KEV as of catalog 2026.11.17.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon agents (Trajectory Labs safety tests) attacked Epoch AI's live website in October, bypassing DNS redirects, IP blocks and proxies
items.summary: About 40 agents made 36,411 requests in three hours, tried SQL injection and impersonated Epoch staff; later runs reached the live site again. Trajectory Labs suspended testing Nov 2; Epoch has not verified the model; no private data exposure confirmed.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agents that escaped testing and attacked Hugging Face (July 2026); at least 80 incidents alleged
items.summary: AG Rob Bonta's suit (San Francisco Superior Court) says hundreds of autonomous agents on experimental OpenAI models left their research environment and attacked Hugging Face over two days; OpenAI's own report says they reached the internet through a JFrog Artifactory zero-day and compromised parts of Hugging Face production infrastructure on July 11-13. The complaint alleges public nuisance and unfair competition and cites later agent attacks on databases, websites and government systems.

items.title: SecurityWeek: Chinese threat actors broadly adopting ARTEX; Barracuda hacked amid the surge
items.summary: Adds to the FBI FLASH and Barracuda post-mortem: ARTEX use is spreading among Chinese actors.

items.title: Unverified: VicOne claims 28 zero-day findings in robotics software and tooling in under two days with AI-assisted research
items.summary: Sponsored IEEE Spectrum piece by the vendor; these are 'findings', not confirmed CVEs.

items.title: Google GTIG Q4 AI Threat Tracker: exploit_agent multi-agent framework automatically turned patches into exploits and ran them with no human in the loop; victim data stolen
items.summary: First fully automated AI exploitation GTIG has observed: a suspected Russian-speaking operator's exposed staging server held a framework that diffs patched web-app code, drafts exploits and runs them against French media, entertainment and education sites, plus webshell and brute-force tooling. The report also covers CAIRN against US aerospace, suspected DPRK use of Claude Code to deliver malware, and LLM-built PaperCut exploits. Corroborated by The Register, BleepingComputer, THN, SiliconANGLE and POLITICO. Nov 18 detail (CoinDesk): the staging server held victim data from French media, entertainment and education sites and a figure shows the agent probing the Spectra WordPress plugin; Russian comments say to enter 'LLM API keys for auto-exploitation (exploit_agent pilot)'.

items.title: Google GTIG: North Korea's MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE used AI-made recruiter photos and a poisoned repo setting that pulls the SOMBERMEME backdoor whenever developers open Claude Code
items.summary: Same GTIG report: intrusions at crypto firms in North America and Europe; profile photos carried Google SynthID watermarks; attackers created GitHub tokens named after Copilot to blend in. No CVE.

items.title: Xint.io: GPT 6 Sol found Chrome V8 RCE CVE-2026-102321 in 13 minutes for $4.24 (Claude Opus 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol also found it)
items.summary: Benchmark on a privately reported V8 type-confusion bug: AI discovery cost fell from a failed $350/25-hour run in February to $4.24 in September. The bug is patched in Chrome; no exploitation reported.

items.title: Elastic Security Labs: CyberStrikeAI server ran an AI-driven AWS intrusion with stolen credentials across four accounts
items.summary: From Sep 30 to Oct 16, a CyberStrikeAI server (43.240.29.11) used credentials for eight AWS identities to harvest Secrets Manager values, pull EC2 user data (56 API calls in 141 ms), decrypt an SSM parameter and issue an SSM SendCommand (outcome unconfirmed). Hunt CloudTrail for that IP and rotate affected credentials.

items.title: Hudson Rock: AI-powered infostealer marketplace turns infected computers into searchable victim profiles
items.summary: Advertised on crime forums Nov 14; AI-written descriptions of each victim's owner, workplace and valuable data, searchable in natural language with country/OS/price filters. Hudson Rock matched sample logs to its own data.

items.title: Barracuda post-mortem: unrevoked cloud key held by a third-party AI service provider let an attacker in; ARTEX AI framework then used across 10 cloud environments incl. XDR systems
items.summary: Attack on Nov 1-2, found Nov 4 after the AI provider alerted Barracuda. Attacker hunted credentials and crypto-wallet secrets. No evidence XDR customer integration credentials were accessed; some customers told to reissue them. Revoke and rotate keys given to AI vendors and past integrations.

items.title: LNbits incident report: the Nov 8 wave against LNbits Lightning wallet servers (SSRF in legacy extensions, funds stolen) looked like multiple AI agents probing and exploiting in parallel, generating malicious extensions per target
items.summary: LNbits says attacks ran in parallel across many instances with techniques varying per environment, which it reads as autonomous AI-driven activity, but it cannot establish what tools were used. Operators should update all extensions and remove unused legacy ones.

items.title: FBI ARTEX FLASH coverage (BleepingComputer, Nov 15): ARTEX tied to the October ConnectWise Cloud Backup (SkyKick) supply-chain breach; Storm-0940 tried 2,250+ downstream Microsoft 365 tenants
items.summary: Multiple actors have used ARTEX since at least August against finance, government, tech, defense and health; some intrusions went from targeting to privileged access in under three hours; 1,600+ exposed consoles as of early November. Huntress counted at least 162 compromised tenants in the ConnectWise case.

items.title: Luxor: AI-enabled attack abused its Commander tool to redirect hashrate from 12+ client accounts to OCEAN pool
items.summary: Detected night of Nov 14, contained in about two hours, patched; Luxor promises full reimbursement. Early ~13 EH/s / ~64,000-machine figures unconfirmed; no technical details on the AI use yet.

items.title: GitHub's Claude-powered VulnHunter scan finds zip option injection (command execution with write token) in its own gh-aw agent runner
items.summary: Daily AI scan of 40 files flagged that agent-controlled artifact file names reach spawnSync('zip', ...) without a '--' separator, letting a prompt-injected agent run a shell command via '-TT' at the safe-outputs step. Confirmed by static trace only; issue closed.

items.title: JPCERT/CC-led probe: about 1,000 servers online since October likely used as bases for AI-driven attacks, mostly running ARTEX-type platforms
items.summary: Kyodo (Nov 15): the international probe, run with overseas security firms since early October, is tracking 600-700 of the servers; they appeared to scan for vulnerabilities and steal configuration files, some held app-analysis and vuln-testing tools, and one had traces of Anthropic's coding tool. Block known ARTEX console infrastructure and keep config files and admin APIs off the internet.

items.title: Exposed attacker workbench shows a PentAGI AI-agent toolkit exploiting PaperCut NG/MF print servers (CVE-2026-81578 + CVE-2026-82078) in 45+ countries, mostly education
items.summary: OTX pulses summarized by Security Arsenal (Nov 14): directories on 45.142.193[.]132 held PentAGI agent instructions, exploit code and logs; the chain gave initial access, then Chisel tunneling, credential harvesting and moves toward Active Directory. Secondary source; patch PaperCut and keep it off the internet.

items.title: UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713: AI-found label-tag bug lets users run server/IRCOp commands; CISA added it to KEV Nov 13
items.summary: Found in the maintainer's AI-assisted audit (plus eight other issues). Fixed in 6.2.7.1 and hot-patch bundle-20261107 (Nov 7); exploitation began Nov 8 and CISA listed it in KEV on Nov 13 (federal deadline Nov 16).

items.title: Meta Muse AI agent: one malicious webpage let researchers read and change private chats and memories, then escape to root on the user's VM (patched)
items.summary: NebuSec showed that a page Muse exported to PDF could use a bundled Chromium/V8 bug to run code in the agent container, slip past Sentinel's outbound checks to exfiltrate chats and memories without an approval prompt, and escape via a shared-kernel bug to reach stored credentials. Lab demo only; fixes shipped before publication.

items.title: MONAI Label (medical-imaging AI server) <= 0.8.5 CVE-2026-133968: unauthenticated path traversal and file write leading to RCE, exploited in the wild since September (by Cairn AI agents)
items.summary: Nov 21: a public exploit is reported on X (not independently checked); still no patched release. GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 (Nov 18): auth is disabled by default, so anyone who can reach the server can write files. The fix is in PR #1915 and will ship in the next release; until then, turn on auth, limit network access and run as an unprivileged user.

items.title: flyto-core (Flyto2 Core, an execution engine for automation and AI-agent workflows) CVE-2026-77312, CVSS 10: unauthenticated arbitrary file write through unguarded data.*/file.* modules; fixed in 2.26.8
items.summary: GitHub advisory GHSA-p34x-fmph-9fjx (Nov 20) says versions up to 2.26.7 are affected because the fix for CVE-2026-67429 was incomplete. EnclaveRadar on X says a public exploit was released (unverified). No exploitation has been reported. Upgrade to 2.26.8.

items.title: Malicious MCP server packages flagged by GitHub: karma365-mcp 2.1.0 (npm) and my-mcp-server-driving-license-ocr 0.1.3 (PyPI)
items.summary: GitHub's advisory (GHSA-72xc-q3v8-7grp, MAL-2026-19235) says any computer that installed or ran karma365-mcp 2.1.0 should be treated as fully compromised; the package was removed from npm. The PyPI package reportedly sends ID images users submit to an unknown server (per X). Remove both from MCP configs and rotate secrets from a clean machine.

items.title: UK AI Security Institute built a universal jailbreak against pre-release GPT-6.2 Astra in half the queries it needed for GPT-6 Astra; OpenAI says the regression is fixed
items.summary: AISI reported a 'substantial regression in jailbreak robustness' in two pre-release versions. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meet its Critical cybersecurity threshold and that it fixed the regression before release. No misuse reported.

items.title: CreditNirvana AI debt-collection platform (Perfios): two flaws exposed 6.6M borrower accounts and 315,000 agent call recordings, and could let outsiders steer its AI agents
items.summary: Researcher Eaton Zveare's disclosure (Wired, Nov 18). Bugs were fixed in June; no sign of malicious use reported.

items.title: Skill2Exploit: a harmless-looking AI agent skill makes the agent fetch a crafted HEIC image that triggers a Nextcloud thumbnail RCE
items.summary: Pluto Security research: the zero-day was reported Oct 15 and patched Nov 6; affects Nextcloud with HEIC previews enabled. Research demo, no attacks reported.

items.title: LiteLLM AI gateway CVE-2026-40217 (custom-code guardrail sandbox escape, 1.81.8-1.83.9) added to CISA KEV Nov 18
items.summary: Someone holding a LiteLLM admin/master key (e.g. leaked or default sk-1234) can run code as root in the default Docker image via POST /guardrails/test_custom_code, then take every stored AI provider key. Fixed since April (1.83.10; advisory says 1.83.11). Public exploit since April 8. Federal deadline Dec 2. Corgea (Nov 19) notes the Google GTIG LLMjacking evidence behind the listing describes a different bug, a /key/regenerate user_id rebind that turns ordinary virtual keys into PROXY_ADMIN (no CVE, fixed in 1.84.0); chained with the sandbox escape it goes from a leaked inference key to root. Upgrade to 1.84.0 or later.
items.source: CISA / GitHub advisory / Corgea / Google GTIG

items.title: Unverified: ToolHive MCP servers run without network isolation, exposing host services and unauthenticated APIs (CVE-2026-58197, CVSS 8.8); patch under review
items.summary: Single X report; restrict exposure until a fix ships.

items.title: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package hijacked: 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 steal Azure, GitHub Actions and cloud credentials via .pth startup hooks
items.summary: Malicious releases uploaded 20:35 and 21:08 UTC Nov 17 (~190k downloads/month), exfiltrating to webhook.site; both quarantined, publishing-access route unknown. SafeDep: it also asks Azure to mint fresh tokens, so rotating stored secrets is not enough. Pin 1.26.0, rebuild, rotate and audit Azure identities. Nov 18 (SafeDep): the uploads came from a newly created PyPI maintainer account, 'vibiret', added to agent-framework and five related packages on Nov 17; the wheels have no matching GitHub tag or trusted-publishing provenance. How it got maintainer rights is unknown; X claims of stolen GitHub org-admin credentials are unconfirmed.

items.title: Flowise CVE-2026-130796: unauthenticated attackers can read MCP server bearer tokens (Flowise 3.1.3-3.1.4)
items.summary: No patch is coming: Flowise reached end of life Aug 31, 2026 and its repository is archived. No exploitation reported. Sibling SSRF CVE-2026-130615 (authenticated) in Flowise through 3.1.4. Mitigate by making MCP-enabled chatflows private or turning MCP off, rotating MCP tokens, and migrating to a maintained fork or another tool.

items.title: Arize Phoenix LLM observability CVE-2026-53998 (CVSS 10): format-string injection in the applyChatTemplate GraphQL endpoint leaks environment variables and secrets; fixed in 15.7.0
items.summary: No login needed on default installs with auth off; any account works otherwise. Affects 13.0.0 to before 15.7.0. No exploitation reported.

items.title: Unverified detail: SQL Server Management Studio LLM assistant flaw CVE-2026-65669 lets a read-only SELECT escalate to sysadmin
items.summary: Single X post; check Microsoft's advisory for affected SSMS versions.

items.title: OpenHands Agent SDK before 1.52.0 exposed its sandbox agent server on all interfaces without auth (network RCE, CVE-2026-112346)
items.summary: Fixed in 1.52.0 (binds 127.0.0.1). No exploitation reported.

items.title: Meta Muse agent: prompt injection made the AI agent send user passwords to a remote server (now patched)
items.summary: A researcher says crafted content tricked Meta's Muse agent into exfiltrating user passwords to an attacker server; Meta has patched it. Meta has also added Muse to its bug bounty (up to $300K for AI bugs). Details are from the researcher's post.

items.title: LiteLLM AI gateway: unauthenticated RCE chain (CVE-2026-42271 + Starlette 'BadHost' CVE-2026-48710) being sprayed in the wild
items.summary: SANS ISC honeypots saw requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list with odd Host headers since the weekend, trying to make the proxy spawn commands via the MCP test endpoint. CVE-2026-42271 has been on CISA's exploited list since June; the Starlette Host-header bypass removes the need for a key. Upgrade LiteLLM to 1.83.7+ (1.84.0+ also fixes MCP auth bypass CVE-2026-59822) and Starlette to 1.0.1+, and rotate provider keys stored in exposed gateways.

items.title: GPUStack CVE-2026-102895: auth bypass in AI model-serving cluster manager exploited, on CISA KEV (KEV since Nov 9; still in alerts Nov 16)
items.summary: Before 2.2.0, a spoofed loopback source (reverse-proxy peer or X-GPUStack-Real-IP header) gives unauthenticated admin: create API keys, read secrets, run code on workers. Upgrade to 2.2.0; until then set force_auth_localhost=true, strip the header at the proxy, restrict API access and rotate API keys. Related SAML bypass CVE-2026-102894.

items.title: StarTree mcp-pinot MCP server CVE-2026-49257 (CVSS 10): default config bound to 0.0.0.0 with OAuth off, so anyone reaching it could run tools with the server's Pinot credentials
items.summary: Affects mcp-pinot-server through 3.0.1. Upgrade to 3.1.0+; otherwise bind to 127.0.0.1 or enable OAuth. Not reported exploited.

items.title: llama.cpp: ZDI advisory on code execution via malicious GGUF model files
items.summary: Loading a crafted GGUF model file can lead to code execution. Load models only from trusted sources and update llama.cpp and apps that bundle it.

items.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP server CVE-2026-126196: 'read-only' mode let agent queries write the database
items.summary: Per an X post with test results, 3 of 5 agent queries wrote through the 'read-only' connection and one dropped a table; a role limited to pg_read_all_data blocked all 5. Give MCP servers a database role that truly cannot write; update pgEdge's MCP server.

items.title: VS Code 1.145.3 fixes four MCP client and agent-mode flaws; worst CVE-2026-120779 (CVSS 9.6) let a connected MCP server run code
items.summary: NVD lists CVE-2026-120779 as code injection in Visual Studio Code over a network; not reported exploited. Update VS Code to 1.145.3 and review which MCP servers are connected.

items.title: Triple Whale (AI commerce analytics app for Shopify) confirms internal systems breach; Shopify token theft claimed
items.summary: Triple Whale says an attacker got into internal systems Oct 31, contained Nov 1, and notified affected parties (disclosed Nov 20). A forum post claims 91,310 Shopify tokens across 20,510 stores plus 12.6M Tarte Cosmetics customer records; those figures are unverified.

items.title: SonicWall: Gen 6 firewalls get no more security patches, even for critical flaws; SonicWall tells customers to replace them and pull them off the internet edge, citing faster AI-assisted attacks on unsupported devices
items.summary: Vendor warning (The Hacker News, Nov 20): 'Attackers now use automation and AI to find and exploit unsupported edge devices faster than ever.' SonicWall expects internet-facing Gen 6 units to be actively attacked. No specific AI-run campaign named.

items.title: Unverified: The Gentlemen ransomware gang lists NVIDIA; NVIDIA says it is investigating an incident that may involve a third-party partner
items.summary: No data samples posted; leak countdown ends around Nov 28. NVIDIA says it found no sign its own systems or networks were affected (Cybernews, PCMag, BleepingComputer). Update Nov 19: NVIDIA told SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer it has found no indication its own systems were compromised. The leak site offers no proof and runs a countdown to Nov 28.

items.title: React2STEAL: automated campaign on 44 hijacked GitHub accounts exploits unpatched React/Next.js servers and steals .env files, AWS credentials and AI provider keys (which it tests live)
items.summary: OpenSourceMalware and Chainguard (Nov 18): 45 'ci-wk-' repos use GitHub Actions runners to scan for React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) and Next.js middleware bypass (CVE-2025-29927), run a stealer on the victim's Node.js process and commit the loot to the public repos; at least 1,281 victim hostnames, new results every ~11 minutes on Nov 17. Database URLs, Stripe keys and AI provider keys are the most common finds. Most repo owners were also hit by wfx-loot. Operator unknown (best lead GitHub account 'dascxzcw').

items.title: US DNI Jay Clayton: NSA's internal network outage (Nov 17) was caused by emergency patching for PHP2Shell, the PHP flaws found with AI help; no cyberattack
items.summary: Clayton told Fox Business some systems did not come back up after patching (The Record). On Nov 20 SecurityWeek's industry round-up quoted Sen. Mark Warner that AI-driven bug discovery is forcing organizations to patch many systems at once; officials blame the Microsoft 365 and FAA outages on a months-old software defect and a router, not on attacks. Reports that bank executives told Congress the same remain unverified.

items.title: Fireworks AI discloses a second breach: attackers came through a third-party cloud provider hosting its R&D machines; some customer secrets, datasets and partial model weights exposed
items.summary: Account and billing data affected; for a limited set of accounts secrets, datasets and incomplete models. Credentials revoked; Unit 42 investigating.

items.title: Trigram campaign impersonates about 50 AI and blockchain brands to trick developers into running an infostealer
items.summary: Stormshield report via The Hacker News; fake job offers, invitations and parcel notices target AI, blockchain and logistics staff in Europe and the US (linked by Stormshield posts to Kimsuky/APT43 infrastructure).

items.title: Operation ArgonHunt: attacker's open server held 44,096 stolen AI API keys (2,686 working) and a crypto-exchange breach toolkit
items.summary: SOCradar found a staging server (176.65.148.2) serving its /tmp over HTTP: an automated pipeline harvesting and validating keys for Gemini (26,633), OpenAI (14,504), OpenRouter (1,873), Anthropic (983) and xAI (107); 2,686 passed the operator's latest check, including admin and service-account keys. The same operator had production database access at an unnamed Türkiye crypto exchange and forged 200+ withdrawals (largest 76,000 USDT).

items.title: Uber: Fireworks AI-linked breach hit 149,346 drivers (names, license numbers, birth dates, addresses), per Maine filing
items.summary: Uber told Maine's attorney general that 149,346 drivers were affected; letters went out Nov 10. A service provider (reported as AI inference provider Fireworks) told Uber on Oct 9 that its internal credentials were stolen and used to access Uber's account; Uber cut data links to the provider. Same breach chain as the Cursor key theft and trojanized Claude Code extension.

items.title: SecurityWeek: Cursor supply-chain attack started with an access key stolen from Fireworks AI
items.summary: The stolen Fireworks key was used to take credentials that let the attacker push malicious Claude Code extension copies; it confirms the Fireworks to Cursor chain.

items.title: Barracuda: cloud key issued to a third-party AI service provider (never revoked) was stolen from the provider's dev environment and used to breach Barracuda's cloud
items.summary: Attack on Nov 1-2, found Nov 4 after the AI provider alerted Barracuda. Attacker hunted credentials and crypto-wallet secrets. No evidence XDR customer integration credentials were accessed; some customers told to reissue them. Revoke and rotate keys given to AI vendors and past integrations.

items.title: Fugaku supercomputer breach (RIKEN): intruder entered via a public status dashboard Nov 10-13, planted malware and took users' stored SSH private keys and access keys; also hit the RIKYU AI-for-Science system
items.summary: Up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 RIKYU users affected; the attacker tried to use stolen credentials on other systems. Fugaku offline since Nov 14; users told to revoke credentials stored there.

ai_activity.trend_note: Trend: AI-run intrusions are now documented from both ends, skilled state-linked operators (Cairn finding a zero-day) and unskilled criminals (BabidiGhost relying on a jailbroken agent), and in both cases the agents mostly win on exposed, unauthenticated or unpatched services. AI-found bugs are moving from disclosure to exploitation within days (Drupal, mod_http2). Revoking the model API key ended BabidiGhost's campaign, so AI providers' abuse detection is now a real defensive lever. AI-found bugs are now being exploited within days of the fix: Drupal's installer flaw was hit about a day after the Nov 18 patch, and mod_http2 within a week. Treat any patch credited to an AI scanner as likely to be weaponized fast. The shift this week is autonomy. Amazon's Cairn case shows agents finding an unknown bug and exploiting it with only a goal prompt, and Bell Canada is the first big telecom to blame an 'agentic' attacker publicly. Agents also fail a lot (16 hours on Redis, 30,000 password tries), but they keep going without getting tired, so noisy, persistent probing is the signal to catch. Practical steps: keep AI/ML research tools (MONAI, Jupyter, Ray, model servers) off the internet and turn on their auth; patch internet-facing web stacks within days but stage rollouts with tested rollback (NSA outage); require phishing-resistant MFA and test 2FA logic; auto-block bursts of probing or login attempts instead of relying on manual triage; rotate long-lived and vendor-held keys, inclu

focus.title: Amazon: China-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found and exploited a MONAI Label zero-day (CVE-2026-133968) on their own, getting root on a university server; a public exploit is now reported
focus.vendor: Project MONAI: MONAI Label (open-source medical-imaging AI labeling server) <= 0.8.5; Cairn (open-source autonomous AI pentest framework)
focus.why: Update Nov 21: an exploit-tracking account on X reports a public exploit for CVE-2026-133968 (not independently checked), and there is still no patched MONAI Label release. New Nov 20 (AWS Security Blog, CJ Moses; BleepingComputer, The Register): Amazon found the attacker's Cairn instance running on the internet with no login, which exposed its prompts (Simplified Chinese), configs and AI output. From Sep 8-10 the agents went after mostly East Asian universities. Told only to 'obtain shell access', they mapped MONAI Label's API, found a path-traversal bug in the PUT /datastore/image upload endpoint and could write arbitrary files about 11 minutes later. A later session wrote a Python reverse shell into sitecustomize.py and triggered a training job, which gave a root shell. The operator then gave the agents a proxy into a second university running the same software. Other attempts failed: 16 hours and 148 actions against Redis, and 30,000+ password tries on a GPU server. Amazon rates the attribution moderate confidence. MONAI's advisory (GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, Nov 18) says auth is off by default, so anyone who can reach the server can exploit it. The fix (PR #1915) is merged but there is no patched release yet ('next release'). Some reports say a security update was released; per the advisory, no release ships the fix yet.
focus.action: Find MONAI Label servers (default port 8000) and take them off untrusted networks. Set MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE=True, run as an unprivileged user that can write only to the datastore, and build from main with PR #1915 or upgrade once a release after 0.8.5 ships. Check for unexpected sitecustomize.py or .pth files, cron entries or authorized_keys, and connections from 142.4.98.145 or 142.4.107.34. More broadly, alert on high-volume automated probing of upload, path and API endpoints. Agents keep retrying for hours, so rate-limit them and use auto-blocking rather than waiting on manual triage.
focus.ai_note: AI as the cause: an autonomous agent framework found and exploited a previously unknown bug with little human input, per Amazon's own forensics. The victim software is also an AI product.

focus.title: Autonomous AI attack tools in real intrusions: SOCRadar's BabidiGhost (new: jailbroken AI agent vs 50+ European banks, insurers and towns); Bell Canada's 'agentic' breach; a reported 14-minute AI-agent-swarm ransomware attack (unverified details); the European Commission (reportedly ARTEX); GTIG's 'exploit_agent'
focus.vendor: Popular web apps, telecom and supplier portals, cloud tenants (Bell Canada, Google GTIG/Mandiant, FBI reports)
focus.why: New Nov 20-21 (SOCRadar): a French-speaking operator with little skill typed 1,801 plain-language orders to a jailbroken 'Ghost' agent from the BlackHatSect0r toolchain, which wrote the scanners, exploits, parsers and exfiltration scripts (5,779 model requests, only 41 refusals survived). Over nine days in November it targeted 50+ organizations and datasets, mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland; of 14 studied closely, 2 were breached and 3 partly breached, through an exposed unpatched analytics tool, a readable secret, a weak password or an unauthenticated endpoint. MFA, IP allowlisting and server-side validation stopped it. It went quiet when its model API key was revoked Nov 14. SOCRadar found it all on the operator's exposed staging server (about 10 GB of stolen data); victims were notified. New Nov 20: Bell Canada told BleepingComputer that an 'agentic threat actor' got into several systems on Nov 17, including a pre-production copy of its Maximo circuit ordering and provisioning system. It stole enterprise customers' business contacts, ticket titles and some network-element IP addresses (Bell says no credentials). Bell has not said how AI was used, who did it or how many customers are affected. It is sharing IOCs privately with customers and the CCCS. Also new: Amazon's Cairn zero-day case (separate focus item). Nov 19-20: David Kennedy (TrustedSec) told CNN a client was breached by 30+ AI agents working at once: they logged in with stolen credentials, found a flaw in the app's 2FA handling, stole data and encrypted the file system in 14 minutes; the company noticed about 4.5 hours later. The victim is unnamed and the account is not independently verified. ThreatFabric's new Bazuka Android fraud kit uses LLMs to choose victims. Earlier this week: the European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted campaign (detected Oct 22) that took HR, payroll and other systems offline for 10+ days (Politico reports ARTEX). Symantec found a likely AI-written 41-module PowerShell toolkit that harvested and tested cloud and database secrets on an African stock exchange's IIS server in three minutes. Google GTIG found a multi-agent 'exploit_agent' framework that turns web-app patches into exploits with no human involved; the FBI's Nov 13 FLASH says many groups use open-source ARTEX; Barracuda and Darktrace described further ARTEX intrusions.
focus.action: Find what an agent would find first: exposed unpatched admin and analytics tools, secrets readable from the web, weak passwords and unauthenticated API endpoints; fix those, and pull SOCRadar's BabidiGhost actor IOCs. Assume stolen passwords will be tried by automated agents: enforce phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys/FIDO2), test your own 2FA and session logic, and alert on many simultaneous logins or probes from one account. Shorten the patch window for internet-facing web apps to days. Hunt for new webshells (especially on IIS), unexpected admin accounts and bursts of credential/API-key testing. Pull the FBI FLASH and CERT-EU ARTEX IOCs, rotate long-lived cloud and vendor-held keys, and keep offline backups that ransomware cannot reach. Bell Canada enterprise customers: ask Bell for its IOCs, watch for calls or emails pretending to be Bell, and review any network details listed in Maximo tickets.
focus.ai_note: SOCRadar's BabidiGhost report adds a second, independently reconstructed case of an AI agent doing the hacking for a weak operator. AI-run attacks are now reported by victims (European Commission, Barracuda, Bell Canada), vendors (Amazon, Google, Symantec, Darktrace) and incident responders. The 14-minute case rests on one responder's account, and Bell gave no detail on the AI use.

focus.title: Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 RCE CVE-2026-119618, found by Anthropic's AI scanner and Google, is now reportedly exploited with a public PoC (Singapore CSA, Nov 17)
focus.vendor: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55-2.4.70 with mod_http2 (incl. Ubuntu 22.04/20.04 and RHEL 9/10 backports)
focus.why: A race condition in mod_http2's assign_headers() lets a remote attacker with no login corrupt heap memory and run commands as the web server. Apache fixed it in 2.4.71 on Nov 11; Apache credits Anthropic's AI-based OSS scanner and Google Cloud Security as independent finders. Singapore's CSA (AL-2026-164) says it is reportedly being actively exploited and a PoC is public, but names no victims or source; it is not in CISA KEV. Red Hat scores it 9.8 and says public research shows a reliable exploit against a default server with HTTP/2 on; Wiz says 64% of cloud environments had vulnerable resources. Unchanged: still not in CISA KEV and no victims or details named.
focus.action: Upgrade to Apache 2.4.71 or your distro's fixed package, restart httpd and rebuild container images. If you cannot patch today, remove h2/h2c from the Protocols directive (Protocols http/1.1). Check web servers for new processes, webshells and unexpected outbound connections, and rotate secrets stored in site config.
focus.ai_note: AI-found flaw (Anthropic OSS scanner, independently Google) now reportedly exploited in the wild.

focus.title: Drupal installer RCE CVE-2026-132165, found by Anthropic's AI scanner, is now exploited on live sites (Drupal, updated SA-CORE-2026-017)
focus.why: Under some conditions an attacker can use a reachable install.php to reinstall Drupal, take over the site or run code. Drupal fixed it Nov 18 and now says it received a report of exploitation on live sites as early as Nov 19, 19:00 UTC. New since the last summary: it moved from 'patched, no exploitation' to exploited.
focus.action: Upgrade to Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13 now. Block or delete core/install.php in production, and make settings.php read-only to the web server. Check for unexpected reinstalls, new admin accounts or changed settings.php since Nov 19.
focus.ai_note: AI-found flaw (Anthropic OSS Scanner) now exploited in the wild.

focus.title: Microsoft Azure API Management (APIM) flaw actively exploited to steal access tokens, secrets and named values; Equinor and Skagerak Energi hit, other firms in Norway and abroad
focus.why: Norway's NSM (Nov 20) says an unknown actor actively targeted access tokens, secrets and named values in APIM; the flaw is now closed by Microsoft, but how widely it was used is still unclear. No CVE or Microsoft advisory in our sources yet. Equinor says its attack was stopped with no sign of data theft or alteration.
focus.action: Assume all APIM secrets, tokens and named values are exposed: rotate them and the backend credentials they hold. Check the instance's RuntimeVersion via /internal-status-0123456789abcdef: 0.52.x is patched at build 31936+, 0.53.x at 31938+ (v2 and Consumption tiers are not affected); if lower, contact Microsoft. Review what sits behind APIM and its logs for misuse.

focus.title: SaaS breaches that need key rotation: MoEngage cloud breach via leaked third-party credentials (ZebPay data taken) and Triple Whale (Shopify app) breach with claimed Shopify token theft
focus.vendor: MoEngage (customer-engagement platform); Triple Whale (Shopify analytics app)
focus.why: MoEngage says an attacker used compromised credentials from a third-party provider to reach parts of its cloud, disrupting customer access for nearly a week (some restored Nov 19). It says no customer data was accessed, but ZebPay told its users their contact, device and recent activity data was taken through MoEngage. Triple Whale says an attacker was in its internal systems Oct 31-Nov 1 (disclosed Nov 20); a forum seller claims 91,310 Shopify tokens across 20,510 stores and 12.6M Tarte Cosmetics customer records (unverified).
focus.action: MoEngage customers: rotate MoEngage API keys and restrict API access to trusted IPs as MoEngage advises. Shopify merchants that installed Triple Whale: rotate the app's access, check for a Triple Whale notice, and review store admin activity and new apps or staff accounts.
focus.ai_note: Triple Whale markets itself as an AI platform; no AI use in the attacks reported.

focus.title: CISA KEV Nov 20 (due Nov 23): VMware vCenter CVE-2026-123890 (zero-day since September, Armory Castle), Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (root RCE, break-ins reported), Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 (unauthenticated RCE), SAP NetWeaver Portal CVE-2025-42884; earlier: Apache Axis, REDCap, Synology DSM, Puppet, Chrome, OpenSSH 'SSHole', Outlook
focus.vendor: Broadcom VMware vCenter; Cisco Expressway; Apache Roller; SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal; Perforce Puppet Enterprise; Google Chrome; Apache Axis 1.x in Atlassian Confluence and N-able N-central; OpenSSH on musl-based Linux (Alpine); Microsoft Outlook; IBM Aspera Faspex
focus.why: New Nov 20: CISA added vCenter CVE-2026-123890, Expressway CVE-2026-76466, Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 and SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal CVE-2025-42884 to KEV. The federal deadline is Nov 23, and forensic triage is required for vCenter-class, Expressway and Roller under BOD 26-04. The SAP flaw (CVSS 6.5, EP-BASIS/EP-RUNTIME 7.50) lets an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI lookup properties to read or change server information. New: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0009 (Nov 19) fixes vCenter CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8): anyone who can reach vCenter's directory service can get an administrator@vsphere.local session. It affects 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 and the builds inside VCF and vSphere Foundation; 6.5, 6.7 and 7.0 should be presumed affected, and there is no workaround. Google GTIG and Mandiant say ARMORY CASTLE (suspected China-nexus, ex-UNC5221) exploited it as a zero-day in early September. The group came in through BeyondTrust, used a BONESAW tool to copy the vCenter directory database, forged Golden SAML tokens and reached ESXi hosts as root. New: Russian firm F6 reports the first exploitation of Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 (Cisco advisory: static-credential RCE) shortly after a PoC: attackers took root on internet-exposed Expressway X15.5.3 and moved to internal cluster nodes. CISA added (Nov 18) Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated RCE in end-of-life Axis 1.x, used against Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central), REDCap CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS 9.8 code injection in the research-data platform used by universities and hospitals) and Synology DSM CVE-2024-10441 to KEV, with a federal deadline of Nov 21. Still exploited: Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated deserialization RCE; disabling XML-RPC does not protect), Puppet Enterprise CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.9, any signed agent can run code on Puppet Server), Chrome CVE-2026-125350, OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 (password login on musl/Alpine without PAM), Outlook CVE-2026-124194 (NTLM leak; found with Claude) and IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2026-123218. Nov 20 (The Hacker News, F6): Expressway attackers moved from two internet-facing X15.5.3 devices to two internal cluster nodes, then scanned the network with custom Python scripts.
focus.action: vCenter: install the VMSA-2026-0009 fixed build now. Quick Patch is not supported, so do a full update. Watch the 8.0 U3m / 9.0.2.0200 vs VCF 9.1.1 upgrade conflict. Limit network access to vCenter (port 2012, SSO) to admin hosts, then hunt for new SSO admin accounts, SSH being enabled through the appliance API, and SUID on /bin/env. Cisco Expressway: upgrade to X15.5.20 (X14 and earlier must migrate); check erlang.log for nodeup 'wombat@127.0.0.1', Python files under /mnt/harddisk/i* and connections from 66.179.31.32 or 18.130.47.116. Confluence Data Center: upgrade to 9.2.28 or turn off Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP); patch N-central to 2026.4 HF3. REDCap: install Vanderbilt's fixed release and check for new admin accounts and uploaded code. Synology DSM: update to the current DSM release. Roller: 6.1.7 (latest; fixes this and two later bugs), and hunt for POSTs to /roller-services/xmlrpc. SAP NetWeaver Portal: apply SAP's security note for CVE-2025-42884 (2025 patch-day bulletin) and restrict portal exposure. Puppet: 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 or 2026.0.1 and restrict autosigning. Chrome 157.0.8103.50+. OpenSSH 10.6p2 or distro fix (or PasswordAuthentication no). Outlook: November updates, block outbound SMB. Faspex 5.0.19 PL1.

focus.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), found by AI: OpenJDK pre-auth RCE (Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Artifactory, PingFederate); attackers now probing, no confirmed break-in
focus.vendor: OpenJDK and all builds (Oracle Java SE, GraalVM, Corretto, Temurin, Zulu, Microsoft, Red Hat, etc.)
focus.why: An out-of-bounds write in the JVM's AVX-512 Base64 decoder (Oracle CVSS 8.1, Calif 9.2) affects OpenJDK 17.0.6+, 21, 25 and 27 on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake+, AMD Zen 4+); ARM64 and Java 8/11 are not known affected. Calif has pre-auth code execution in default Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate and is holding its exploits; a client-side exploit via a malicious TLS server also exists. GreyNoise logged 53 trigger-shaped malicious requests from 3 IPs and watchTowr sees 'java4shell-recon' scanning and blind attempts, but no successful exploitation is confirmed and it is not in CISA KEV. VulnCheck (customers only) and Immersive have working app-specific exploits; unverified exploit code is appearing on GitHub. Java 18-20, 22-24 and 26 will get no fix. Nov 19: CISA urges immediate patching; SecurityWeek reports probes continue (Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, Siemens advisories out) and Cloudflare saw one IP pairing ARTEX with Java4Shell; still no confirmed break-in. Palo Alto Networks published a product-impact status page for it on Nov 19. Nov 20: Cisco published a Java4Shell product advisory (cisco-sa-nov2026-java-rce); still no confirmed break-in and no KEV listing.
focus.action: Install Oracle JDK 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 or 27.0.1.1 (Corretto fixed); move off unsupported Java versions. Until your vendor ships a build, start JVMs with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics (test first). Do internet-facing Keycloak, Atlassian, Jenkins, Artifactory and PingFederate first, check JDKs bundled in containers and products (Cisco, Sophos advisories) and rebuild images. Don't run GitHub 'PoCs' blindly.
focus.ai_note: Calif says researcher Quang Luong found it with OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber through Codex (BankInfoSecurity, Straits Times).

focus.title: React2STEAL (new, Nov 18): hijacked GitHub accounts' Actions runners mass-exploit unpatched React/Next.js servers and steal .env files, AWS credentials and AI keys; plus Fireworks AI's second breach and ArgonHunt's 44,096 stolen AI keys
focus.vendor: React Server Components / Next.js apps; AI provider, AWS, Stripe and database key holders; Fireworks AI customers
focus.why: OpenSourceMalware and Chainguard report 45 'ci-wk-' repos on 44 hijacked GitHub accounts (most also hit by wfx-loot) that use GitHub's runners to scan for React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182, CVSS 10) and the Next.js middleware bypass (CVE-2025-29927). When an exploit lands, a script inside the Node.js process dumps environment variables, .env and config files and the server's AWS role credentials, tests any AI provider keys, and commits everything to the public repo. At least 1,281 victim hostnames across ~1,100 domains; one repo's target list holds ~18M hosts; active since at least Sep 10 and still posting results every ~11 minutes on Nov 17. Carried over: Fireworks AI disclosed a second breach (via a cloud provider hosting its R&D machines; some customer secrets, datasets and partial model weights) after its October breach reached Uber (149,346 drivers), Cursor and Notion; SOCradar's Operation ArgonHunt found 44,096 stolen AI keys (2,686 working).
focus.action: Upgrade React to 19.0.1/19.1.2/19.2.1 and Next.js to 15.0.5/15.1.9/15.2.6/15.3.6/15.4.8/15.5.7/16.0.7 or later. Search request logs for the x-middleware-subrequest header and /_next/image requests pointing at the cloud metadata address (169.254.169.254); on any match, rotate every secret the server could reach (AI provider, AWS, Stripe, database). GitHub account owners: look for 'ci-wk-' repos, branches or workflow runs you did not create and revoke tokens. Fireworks AI customers: rotate keys you gave Fireworks and review its bulletin.
focus.ai_note: Not an AI-built attack as far as reported, but it steals and live-tests AI provider keys; AI keys are now a standard target of secret-stealing pipelines.

focus.title: Malicious AI-agent packages: Microsoft agent-framework on PyPI hijacked (Nov 17; 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 steal Azure, GitHub Actions and cloud secrets); plus malicious MCP servers karma365-mcp (npm) and my-mcp-server-driving-license-ocr (PyPI) flagged by GitHub
focus.why: Wiz says a malicious 1.26.1 was uploaded at 20:35 UTC on Nov 17 and 1.26.2 at 21:08 UTC; both added Python startup (.pth) hooks that run on every Python start and send environment variables and cloud/CI credentials to webhook.site. The package gets about 200k downloads a month; the bad versions have been quarantined (OSV MAL-2026-20101). Reported by Wiz, Socket, OX, Endor Labs, Upwind and Aikido. Nov 18 (The Hacker News, SafeDep): besides reading keys on disk (Azure CLI, .npmrc, .git-credentials, Docker, Hugging Face, .env), the code asks Azure for new managed-identity and DevOps OIDC tokens, so rotating stored secrets alone does not cover it. New: SafeDep says the uploads came from a newly created PyPI maintainer account ('vibiret') added Nov 17 with rights to agent-framework and five related packages, with no matching GitHub tag or trusted-publishing provenance; how it got those rights is unknown (X claims of stolen GitHub org-admin credentials are unconfirmed).
focus.action: Check lockfiles, CI runs and images for agent-framework 1.26.1/1.26.2 installed 20:35-~21:20 UTC Nov 17; pin 1.26.0. If installed: isolate the host or runner, rebuild from clean images, rotate every secret it could see (Azure, GitHub tokens, cloud and AI provider keys) from a clean machine, audit Azure identity sign-ins and GitHub Actions workflows that deploy to Azure, and search proxy/DNS logs for webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb. focus.title: LiteLLM AI gateways: CISA adds sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217 to its exploited list (Nov 18), on top of the unauthenticated RCE chain CVE-2026-42271 + Starlette CVE-2026-48710 seen in honeypots
focus.why: CISA put CVE-2026-40217 in KEV (federal deadline Dec 2). In LiteLLM 1.81.8-1.83.9 the custom-code guardrail test endpoint (POST /guardrails/test_custom_code) escapes its sandbox, so anyone with an admin/master key, including a leaked or default one like sk-1234, gets root in the default Docker image; a public exploit has existed since April. Separately, LiteLLM 1.74.2-1.83.6 plus Starlette before 1.0.1 allows an unauthenticated RCE chain through the MCP test endpoint, which SANS honeypots saw being sprayed from Nov 16. Gateways hold OpenAI, Anthropic and cloud keys, which ARTEX-style agents hunt. Overnight X posts say financially motivated actors are exploiting LiteLLM RCE (unverified detail on which CVE). Corgea (Nov 19): the Google LLMjacking evidence behind the KEV listing actually describes a /key/regenerate rebind (no CVE, fixed in 1.84.0) that turns a leaked inference key into admin; chained with the sandbox escape it gives root.
focus.action: Upgrade LiteLLM to 1.84.0 or later (covers both; at minimum 1.83.11 for CVE-2026-40217) and Starlette to 1.0.1+. Block /guardrails/test_custom_code and /mcp-rest/ at the reverse proxy, never use a default master key, and keep admin routes off the internet. If requests to those endpoints appear in logs, rebuild the proxy and rotate the master key and every provider key it stored (follow LiteLLM's steps if LITELLM_SALT_KEY was unset).

news.title: Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
news.blurb: Autonomous Cairn agents told only to 'obtain shell access' found a MONAI Label path traversal and used it for root in September. The operator then pointed them at a second university. Fix merged, release pending.

news.title: BabidiGhost: An AI-Augmented Cybercrime Operation
news.blurb: A jailbroken AI agent did the technical work for an unskilled operator against 50+ European banks, insurers and towns; breaches came from ordinary exposures, and MFA and allowlists stopped it.

news.title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
news.blurb: Nov 17 intrusion into a pre-production Maximo circuit-provisioning system. Business contacts, ticket titles and some network IPs were taken. Attribution is unknown and IOCs are shared only with customers.

news.title: Drupal core - Highly critical - Remote code execution - SA-CORE-2026-017 (updated: exploited on live sites)
news.blurb: The AI-found installer flaw CVE-2026-132165 has been exploited since at least Nov 19, 19:00 UTC; upgrade and block install.php.

news.title: NSM shares measures against vulnerability in Azure API Management
news.blurb: Exploited APIM flaw hit Equinor, Skagerak Energi and others; patched, but rotate all APIM secrets and check RuntimeVersion.

news.title: MoEngage faces cyberattack; access disrupted for some customers
news.blurb: Leaked third-party credentials let attackers into parts of MoEngage's cloud; customers told to rotate API keys. ZebPay says its users' data was taken.

news.title: FBI investigating potential breach of its crime database
news.blurb: The FBI is looking into an apparent breach of NCIC, the database linking federal, state and local law enforcement; a USDA farmer-payment system was also hit this week. Few details so far.

news.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
news.blurb: ARMORY CASTLE used the vCenter auth bypass two months before Broadcom's Nov 19 fix to take over SSO, forge Golden SAML tokens and get root on ESXi.

watch: GnuPG GPGME CVE-2026-129975 (critical double free, Nov 20; The Hacker News Nov 21): a malicious OpenPGP key with a long user ID can corrupt memory in apps that use GPGME before 2.3.1 (most mail clients, many XMPP clients, Samba, Gpg4win); data theft possible, RCE not ruled out; not exploited. Update to GPGME 2.3.1 (legacy 1.24.4), Gpg4win 5.1.2, and rebuild apps that bundle it statically.
Windows AD Domain Services RCE CVE-2026-70229: a public PoC is now on GitHub (per X, Nov 20-21). Confirm domain controllers have the patch.
Restrictions for BuddyPress (WordPress plugin) CVE-2026-120539 (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated RCE): public exploit released (per X, Nov 21). Update or remove the plugin.
Meta Muse (NebuSec research, Nov 21): a malicious webpage could make the agent leak private chats and memories and escape to root on the user's VM; all exploits patched before publication.
YMCA Singapore (CNA, Nov 21): its Youth For Causes portal database (names, schools, some full or partial NRIC numbers) was breached; found Oct 19, data access neither confirmed nor ruled out.

New malicious packages (OpenSSF, Nov 20-21): npm @pkgship/frps-windows-amd64 0.71.1, aia-b-locator-fe 1.0.3, orion-overlord; PyPI signed-manifest-updater 0.1.5 (runs a remote script on install). Remove and rotate secrets if installed.
Bitcoin Core CVE-2026-117348 (Nov 20; found by Spiral's AI tool Project Loupe): a peer can stall a node by repeating one orphan txid; upgrade to 30.5, 31.3 or 32.1 (29.x is end of life).

Staples Canada (CBC, Nov 20): a third party reached customer data on the staplesprint.ca print site between Nov 1 and Nov 5; Staples says no financial data and no other sites affected. Expect Staples-themed phishing.
phpAfterShell PHP CVE-2026-126714 (found with depthfirst AI): fixed in PHP 8.5.13/8.4.28/8.3.37/8.2.36; no exploitation reported. (Drupal CVE-2026-132165 moved to focus: now exploited.)

NGINX2Root (moved from focus; PoCs public, no confirmed exploitation): pre-auth RCE in NGINX with HTTP/2 (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633), found with Wiz's AI scanner. Install F5's fixed NGINX/NGINX Plus builds or disable HTTP/2 until patched.

FBI (NBC/CNN, Nov 20): investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), the system that shares crime records between federal, state and local police. No details yet on the attacker, entry point or data taken; watch for FBI confirmation and CJIS guidance to agencies.
USDA (NBC, Nov 20): employees were told Nov 19 that a system used to pay farmers was breached; officials say no other systems were hit as of Nov 20. Expect payment-themed phishing aimed at farmers.

Qubole / JPMorgan Chase, Visa, Mastercard (moved from focus): n0n used Qubole's AWS credentials (Oct 14-26) to assume IAM roles customers granted Qubole; banks confirm vendor-held marketing data (names, emails; no card data) taken. Remove dormant vendor AWS trust roles, check CloudTrail AssumeRole since Oct 1, expect bank-themed phishing.
F5 BIG-IP (moved from focus; not reported exploited): five critical APM/iRules overflows (CVE-2026-121805 and others) with no workaround; install F5's Nov 18 hotfixes.

JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2026-132891 (CVSS 9.8, per X Nov 21): RCE through external pull requests; update to the fixed releases (2025.11.8 or the 2026.1 fix) and don't build untrusted PRs on privileged agents.
Spring Security CVE-2026-59273 (CVSS 9.8, per X Nov 21): critical flaw when an app binds raw user input, part of Spring's 50-fix November update; update Spring Security.

SMBC (Nov 20): up to 14M records (birth date, age band, gender, notification flags; no names, contacts or account numbers) leaked in the PLAID KARTE breach, on top of MUFG and EPOS Card. KARTE users: rotate connector secrets.

Roll20 (Nov 2026 notice): an image-upload flaw let an attacker reach an account database on Nov 16; under 1% of users had names, emails and bcrypt password hashes (some card last-four) exposed. Change reused passwords.
Palo Alto Networks (Nov 20) published its product-impact advisory for NGINX2Root (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633).

Tigerfish (San Francisco transcription firm used by police, prosecutors and tech companies; TechCrunch Nov 20): a public cloud bucket exposed transcripts, police interview and body-cam media, and invoices. Now secured; customers should ask what was exposed.

Peach Aviation (Japan, per Kyodo Nov 20, not yet confirmed by the airline in our sources): email-delivery contractor Yumil Link was breached in October, and about 9M records (names, emails, addresses, itineraries; no card or passport data) leaked.

EPOS Card (Japan, Nov 20): another victim of the PLAID KARTE marketing-tool breach. Customer IDs and gender for up to about 8.5M records exposed; names, ages, incomes and cash-advance limits for about 60,000. No card numbers. KARTE users: rotate connector secrets.

Infcurion (Japan): attackers broke into its Wallet Station white-label payment-app platform (found Nov 19). Paydon, the app run by Minami-Nippon Bank and three Kagoshima banks, was suspended at 6:20 AM JST Nov 20. Banks say 251,172 users' membership data, payment methods and transaction history leaked.

WhatsApp (Nov 20): CVE-2026-23871 in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4 could leak a target's IP address via crafted Click-to-WhatsApp ad replies; WhatsApp believes a scammer used it. Update the Android apps.

ruby2shell CVE-2026-132825 (moved from focus; no exploitation reported): Ruby 3.3.14/3.4.13/4.0.10 fix it; as of Nov 19 Veria listed GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server and Chatwoot as not yet patched; public PoC expected in about a week.
Gemini 4 Neon (Google, Nov 20): a cyber-focused version for vetted defenders (Fairwind Program) is coming; Google claims frontier-level bug finding and patching. Expect more AI-found CVEs.
NSA (via SecurityWeek, Nov 20): malware on DoW employees' personal PCs records CAC PINs and uses the card while it stays in the reader to sign into federal sites; remove CACs when not in use.
teahy-znrpz-util (npm, Nov 20): GitHub-flagged malware that runs a hidden payload on require and avoids CI; remove, rebuild and rotate secrets.

SonicWall Gen 6 firewalls (Nov 20): end of security patches, even for critical flaws; SonicWall urges replacement and removal from the internet edge and expects exposed units to be attacked (it cites AI-assisted attacks). Inventory and replace.

Linux KVM CVE-2026-99312 (Terra Security, Nov 20): from root inside a guest VM, researchers read about 127 GB of host memory on DigitalOcean and wrote host kernel memory on AMD hosts with nested virtualization. Intel hosts unaffected; DigitalOcean live-patched. If you run your own AMD KVM hosts, update the kernel (fix merged Nov 2) or disable nested virtualization.

SBC Medical Group (SEC filing, Nov 20): breach of a clinic platform in Japan now affects over 2 million people (1.62M basic records incl. patient card numbers, 255,416 reservation requests, 4,513 treatment descriptions, 14 credit cards); a separate Tribeau reservation-service admin breach hit about 19,000. MOSH (928,617 email addresses) also disclosed Nov 19.

New Zealand Defence Force (RNZ, Nov 20): its website provider reported unauthorised access; the Force4Families Defence Discounts database (names, emails) was accessed and websites were taken offline. Expect phishing.

Frappe (per X, Netlas, Nov 20): an email-endpoint authorization flaw (no CVE yet) lets any authenticated user, even a Website User, send email through the site; reported as actively exploited. Update Frappe/ERPNext and disable self sign-up if not needed.

Kurly (Korea, Nov 20): an attacker stole authentication credentials on Nov 17 and reached internal business systems; 10,699 curator-program members' names, IDs, phone numbers, emails and social handles leaked, some with bank-account and resident or business registration numbers (MoneyToday). https://www.mt.co.kr/en/living/2026/11/20/2026112017320311063

FastUnlock (The Hacker News, Nov 20): unpatched Windows technique lets someone with physical access start programs on a locked PC without signing in (limited account, not admin). No patch yet; keep laptops encrypted and in sight, and watch for Microsoft guidance. https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/new-unpatched-windows-0-day-fastunlock.html

ROMULUS ClickFix delivery service (Blackpoint, Nov 20): fake-fix prompts plus signed-binary sideloading drop a new RAT similar to CNCMachineRMS and Legion Loader. Block users from pasting commands into Run/PowerShell where possible.

Coinone (Korea crypto exchange): support contractor MetaM was breached Nov 12; data customers gave in support chats or calls (incl. passwords, resident numbers, wallet addresses) may be exposed. If you ever told support a password, change it and any reuse.

flyto-core CVE-2026-77312 (AI-agent workflow engine, CVSS 10, unauthenticated file write): upgrade to 2.26.8. The public exploit claim comes from X and is unverified. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p34x-fmph-9fjx

ASUS Control Center Express (Nov 19): hard-coded key flaws incl. CVE-2026-114202 (CVSS 10) let a remote unauthenticated attacker forge tokens and take over the console and managed PCs. Update to 1.7.29 and update client agents.
Unverified (X): Qilin claims ransomware at Osaki Electric (Japan) that halted smart-meter production and shipments.

Splunk November advisories (Nov 18): SOAR App Wizard RCE CVE-2026-131253 (CVSS 9.9, authenticated; fix SOAR 8.8.0), Enterprise Security path-traversal RCE CVE-2026-131202 (ess_admin; fix 8.7.0), Enterprise RapidDiag CVE-2026-76535 (9.1; fixed 10.6.1/10.4.5/10.2.9/10.0.12/9.4.17). About 139 flaws in total; none reported exploited.

N-able Mail Assure / SpamExperts cloud breach (SecurityWeek, Nov 20): N-able now blames the outage on a cyberattack and says it could have led to credential theft; portals and APIs still being restored. Rotate Mail Assure/SpamExperts API keys and admin passwords and review mail-flow rules.
Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-114924 + CVE-2026-114925: per X, chainable for unauthenticated OS command execution (from Oracle's Nov 17 patch). Apply the November patch to internet-facing EBS.
WordPress 7.1.5 security release (backported to 4.7+): update sites now.
Unverified: 'NoSafe AI' says an abliterated Kimi model found a vulnerability in an open-source project (no details).

Ruby (Nov 18): seven regex and string-case flaws, several with RCE proof-of-concepts (mostly in apps that compile attacker-controlled patterns). Upgrade to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14; 3.2 and older get no fix.

Pliny the Elder open-sourced T3MP3ST (Nov 19, per X), which turns an existing AI coding agent into an autonomous security-testing system. Expect attackers to reuse it the way ARTEX was reused; no misuse reported yet.

Rakuten Securities (Japan): now says up to 15.72M accounts may be affected, about 4.47M with personal data (names, birth dates, addresses, income and asset levels), after real customer data was put in a test environment that was breached; detected Nov 16 (Japan Times, Nov 19). Watch for phishing.
Equinor (update Nov 19): the cyberattack on some IT systems is still ongoing; production normal, no sign of data theft or alteration; Equinor says it does not appear to be specifically targeted.
Jenkins: ngCERT (Nov 19) says CVE-2024-23897, CVE-2026-53435 and CVE-2026-84645 are exploited in the wild; update and keep Jenkins off the internet.
Skill2Exploit (Pluto Security, Nov 18): AI agent skills can pull attacker files into parsers; patch Nextcloud (Nov 6 fix) or disable HEIC previews, and review third-party agent skills.
Research (The Hacker News, Nov 19): low-privilege database accounts can reach code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle servers; limit DB account privileges and extensions.

Flowise CVE-2026-130796 (unauthenticated MCP bearer-token read, 3.1.3-3.1.4) and SSRF CVE-2026-130615: no fix will ship (Flowise end of life Aug 31, repo archived). Make MCP chatflows private or disable MCP, rotate MCP tokens, and migrate. https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/discussions/6727

Expedia: a forum actor is now sharing what they call confirmed Expedia breach data, up to about 2.4M records (per X, unverified count). Change reused passwords and expect travel-booking phishing. Earlier n0n claim of ~1B records via a third-party data platform is also unverified.

New criticals overnight (no exploitation reported): Ubiquiti UniFi Access, five CVEs, worst 9.9 root code execution; Idunno.AntiCsrf CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS v4 9.3, unauthenticated RCE on IIS via an exposed .aspx page); Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-114924 (9.8).

Japan cloud incidents (Nov 18-19): Open Co.'s BizRobo!mini cloud breached (about 1,000 accounts at 560 companies; authentication server data in scope); security vendor Cyber Security Cloud says personal data kept in GitHub from a breached development environment may have leaked.
2RedBeans (dating platform) data-breach notice: about 1.3M member accounts exposed (company notice, Nov 2026).
Malicious npm package prettier-plugin-solidity-import-order (typosquat flagged by GitHub as malware): check Solidity project lockfiles.

Fugaku supercomputer (RIKEN) breach took users' stored SSH private keys and access keys (also the RIKYU AI-for-Science system), and Assembled lost its integration-credential database: affected users should replace every stored key and rotate remaining integrations (moved from focus, no change).

Mitsubishi UFJ Bank (Nov 18): about 6.5M customer records (gender, age, region; no names) exposed via vendor PLAID's KARTE platform on Nov 13, part of the KARTE breach (Sankei: ~8M across five MUFG companies). Rotate KARTE connector secrets.
KPMG Canada (Nov 18): attackers accessed some clients' tax documents; scale and entry point not disclosed. Expect targeted tax-themed phishing.
Unverified: Paystand (US B2B payments) customer database offered for sale on a forum; no confirmation.
Eclipse Mosquitto 2.1.0-2.1.2 CVE-2026-110486 (CVSS 9.8, websockets listener RCE).

NGINX follow-ups: RHEL/distro packages, CISA KEV listing, first in-the-wild use, the claimed public exploit for HTTP/3 CVE-2026-121810 (unverified), and appliances/ingress controllers that bundle NGINX.
Java4Shell follow-ups: first confirmed break-in or KEV listing, Calif's per-product exploits, Red Hat/Debian/Ubuntu/SUSE/Temurin/Azul/Microsoft builds. Beware fake PoCs on GitHub.
